nodes.description: An HLA-matched cord-blood transplant in one boy at approximately 4.5 years normalized leukocyte enzyme activity and reduced urinary oligosaccharides. Early neurological worsening partly improved, but the developmental gap persisted and memory declined by two years. Follow-up of the same patient in 2025 documented renewed motor regression and worsening spasticity/ataxia. This does not establish durable neurological efficacy or routine use; biochemical correction is not a validated surrogate for clinical benefit.

nodes.description: The inherited caprine disorder reproduces beta-mannosidase deficiency, oligosaccharide storage and prenatal myelin deficits. This does not distinguish altered proliferation from cell death or establish oligodendrocyte death in humans. Neonatal regional substrate measurements did not track the severity of myelin loss.
